root_cause.text: The libceph OSD client did not reset its sparse-read reply state machine (`o_sparse_op_idx` / `o_sparse_read` in `osd_client.c`) when `osd_fault()` handled a dropped connection, so retried reads could reuse stale sparse-read state and misparse the next reply as a continuation of the previous one, leading to a stuck error loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `osd->o_sparse_op_idx = -1;` and `ceph_init_sparse_read(&osd->o_sparse_read);` in `osd_fault()`, and the CVE description states that if a connection is lost mid-payload or the sparse-read state machine errors, “the sparse-read state is not reset” and “the OSD client will then interpret the beginning of a new reply as the continuation of the old one.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Reset sparse read tracking during OSD fault handling so recovery starts from a clean state.
intent_record.what: Two statements were inserted in osd_fault(): it now assigns -1 to osd->o_sparse_op_idx and calls ceph_init_sparse_read(&osd->o_sparse_read) before attempting to reopen the OSD and kick requests.
intent_record.how: On an OSD connection fault, the sparse read operation tracking and sparse read state are reset before recovery proceeds, preventing stale sparse-read state from carrying over across the fault/reopen path.

grouping_result.intent: Reset sparse read tracking during OSD fault handling so recovery starts from a clean state.

This resumes outstanding OSD requests after fault handling. Without clearing sparse-read state first, these retried requests can reuse stale sparse-read parsing state and get stuck in an error loop.
